facts.value: Shinto is the ever-nebulous religion of Japan with no settled doctrine or origin story.
Kami are the personified concepts of wind, rivers, trees, and other natural elements.
During WWII, the Japanese government instituted Shinto as a state religion that aimed to venerate the emperor as a living, human kami.
Shinto beliefs have developed since the 6th century as a nature-focused series of scattered beliefs that merged and then split with Buddhism as well as Confucianism.
Shinto focuses on ancestry and nature, understood through Japanese storytelling, with a recognition of the horror of 20th-century industry threatening the magic of the world.
